name: Real-time clock DS3231 (I2C)
description: Battery-backed real-time clock with a temperature-compensated crystal, on I2C at 0x68. Wire GND → GND, VCC → 5V, SDA → A4, SCL → A5 on an Uno and use RTClib (RTC_DS3231 rtc; rtc.begin(); rtc.now()). The simulated clock starts at the startTime prop and runs with simulation time, so every run is reproducible.

pins.label: 32K
pins.description: 32.768 kHz output (open drain). Not modelled: stays high-impedance.

pins.label: SQW
pins.description: Square wave / alarm interrupt output (open drain, active low). Not modelled: stays high-impedance.

pins.label: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock. Uno: A5. 4.7 kOhm pull-up on the module.

pins.label: SDA
pins.description: I2C data. Uno: A4. 4.7 kOhm pull-up on the module.

props.label: Time at t = 0
props.description: Clock time when the simulation starts. The options are presets; to set any other time while running, set the 'time' field (interaction set, key 'time', value 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS'), or let the sketch call rtc.adjust().

props.label: Temperature
props.description: Die temperature the RTC reports (registers 0x11/0x12, 0.25 °C steps).

props.label: Lost power
props.description: Start with the oscillator-stop flag set, as after the backup battery ran out (RTClib rtc.lostPower() returns true).

footprint: 38 x 22 mm ZS-042 module, 6-pin 0.1 in header, CR2032 holder

bindings.description: HH:MM:SS shown on the module drawing.
Powered (a real DS3231 keeps time on its battery, but answers I2C only when powered).
